summary: Octagonal granite light first built on Goat Island in 1823, moved to Sandy Point in 1851-52 and first lit there January 17, 1852. Lost its keeper's dwelling in the 1938 hurricane.

structures.note: Re-erected at Sandy Point from the 1823 Goat Island tower; nomination gives 28 feet, LighthouseFriends thirty feet
One and a half story clapboard keeper's dwelling; destroyed in the 1938 hurricane and not rebuilt

access.note: LighthouseFriends: grounds open, tower closed. The US Lighthouse Society archive lists the station as not open to the public.

events.note: Tower built on Goat Island, Newport Harbor (NRHP; LighthouseFriends)
Goat Island light first lit January 1, 1824 (NRHP)
Abandoned after a nearby new light was completed (NRHP). LighthouseFriends says discontinued in 1842. Sources disagree.
Congress appropriates $3,500 for a lighthouse on Prudence Island, September 28, 1850 (LighthouseFriends)
Goat Island tower taken down, moved to Sandy Point and rebuilt; contract of $900 awarded to Horace Vaugh (NRHP) or Horace Vaughn (LighthouseFriends), October 15, 1851
Fifth-order Fresnel lens replaces the Winslow Lewis lamps (LighthouseFriends)
Fog bell with automatic striking mechanism established August 10, 1884 (LighthouseFriends)
September 21 hurricane; keeper's wife and son, a former keeper and two guests drown when the dwelling is destroyed
All station structures except the tower destroyed (NRHP)
Light automated the year after the storm (NRHP). LighthouseFriends dates automation to 1961.
Automation date given by LighthouseFriends; a few island residents tended the light until then
Fog bell removed and replaced by a diaphragm horn on the lantern gallery (NRHP)
Coast Guard gives the American Lighthouse Foundation a twenty-year caretaker contract (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett)
Caretaker contract passes to the Prudence Island Conservancy after local protests
Ownership transferred to the Prudence Conservancy (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett)

corrections.why: The present Prudence Island light was first lit at Sandy Point on January 17, 1852. The 1823 tower was first lit on Goat Island (NRHP: lit January 1, 1824). The record's 1823 describes the Goat Island tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1823 tower built on Goat Island was taken down and rebuilt at Sandy Point in 1851-52 (NRHP; LighthouseFriends). The present tower dates from 1851 (plaque) and the light was first lit there in 1852. The 1823 and 1824 dates belong to the Goat Island tower.

notes_for_editor: 1) Automation date: NRHP says automated 1939 (the year after the 1938 hurricane); LighthouseFriends says residents tended the light until automation in 1961; the USLHS lamplighter roster runs to 1972. Not settled; the facts entry uses 1961 and the event list carries both. 2) Ownership: LighthouseFriends' history reports the 2024 transfer to the Prudence Conservancy, but its visitor notes say the Coast Guard owns the light and leases it to the Conservancy. Rowlett says the 2024 transfer was carried out. 3) Range: the record has 6.0 nm; the nomination says 'a range of 9 miles' with no unit stated. Not put in facts. 4) Lens: the archive's 'Original Optic Type' is fifth-order Fresnel; LighthouseFriends dates its installation to 1855 (the record's 1852 lens event is the archive's first-light year); the present optic is listed as 250 mm. The lens 'status' is unknown. 5) Dwelling distance: nomination 200 feet, LighthouseFriends 190 feet. 6) Goat Island abandonment: nomination 1838, LighthouseFriends discontinued 1842; the Newport Harbor Light story treats the same question. 7) Spellings: the nomination prints Vaugh (sic), the archive and LighthouseFriends print Vaughn; the archive spells Henry Diman, LighthouseFriends Dimond. 8) The Bulletin 1938 passage is OCR'd from a two-column page: the former keeper's name is OCR'd as Martin Thomas, so the story uses the name from LighthouseFriends and the archive (Martin Thompson, 1905-1933) and does not quote the OCR. Quotations from the Bulletin are as OCR'd; the checker should read PDF page 39 for the wording. 9) Bulletin 1922, PDF page 7 (garbled two-column list) appears to record a change at Prudence Island from oil to acetylene, fixed to flashing; LighthouseFriends dates the flashing characteristic to 1924. Not used in the story; check the page image before relying on it. 10) The archive lists two contractors, David Melville and Horace Vaughn, under 'Contractor' with no years; they are not keepers and are not in the roster. 11) The Lighthouse Board annual reports in the local corpus begin in 1891, so the 1850s-1880s rest on the nomination, LighthouseFriends and the archive. 12) Several named lamplighters (Michael J. Bachini, Marcy Bachini Dunbar, Roger C. Grant) served after about 1960 and may be living. They are named only as the archive prints them, with years and role, and no other personal detail is used. 13) George T. Gustavus's later Coast Guard and Nobska/Chatham service is from LighthouseFriends; other_stations entries cite LighthouseFriends. 14) No general period context is used; the story needed none. 15) No photos added. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the Bulletin's 1938 page reads the former keeper's name as 'Martin Thomas' (OCR); the story uses Martin Thompson from LighthouseFriends and the archive, and does not quote the OCR name. The gender statements about the lamplighters were removed because no source gives them.
